title: Advocacy for Disabilities Run Awry
author: Special Education Today
summary: This short Special Education Today post critiques an early-2000s public service announcement from the Coordinated Campaign for Learning Disabilities, arguing that the video, despite its good intentions, perpetuated a persistent and unfounded myth about learning disabilities. The author explains that the PSA implied letter and number reversals are diagnostic indicators of dyslexia or a learning disability, a claim not supported by the research on LD identification. Beyond the content critique, the author raises secondary concerns about the video's murky copyright status and the apparent disappearance of the Coordinated Campaign for Learning Disabilities as an organization. The piece closes by previewing a planned series sharing 10 to 12 more archival PSA spots from the same campaign, framing the exercise as a useful historical record of how disability advocacy operated two decades ago, warts and all. Though brief, the post makes a substantive evidence-based point relevant to teachers and parents: well-intentioned public messaging about disabilities can itself spread misconceptions that outlive the campaign that created them.
points: Identifies letter/number reversal as a persistent but evidence-unsupported myth about dyslexia and learning disability identification, despite its use in official advocacy messaging.

Notes the specific real-world consequence: framing normal developmental reversals (like mixing up phone number digits) as disability indicators risks unnecessary parental alarm or misdiagnosis assumptions.
Raises a secondary provenance concern: the PSA's unclear copyright status and the disappearance of the sponsoring organization's web presence.
Frames the exercise as historical documentation, previewing a planned series of 10-12 more archival disability-advocacy PSAs for critical review.
quotes: The Coordinated Campaign for Learning Disabilities collaborated with the US-based Advertising Council, a non-profit organization that promotes public service efforts, to air a series of brief media—television and radio—about learning disabilities.
This video perpetuated an unfounded description of dyslexia and LD. Reversals of letters and numerals (and transposition of letters and numbers) are not indicators of LD.
Mixing up the order of digits in a phone number is not an indicator that the mixer-upper has LD! It's a myth. We should help the public learn this.
I've been searching for copyright information for this and other videos (and radio spots) in the series published by Coordinated Campaign for Learning Disabilities.

I have original copies of 10-12 more of these spots. I shall be sharing them over the coming months, as I think it is valuable for we denizens of SETland to see how some advocacy was happening in the early 2000s.
